issues.legal_issue: A claim that an entire building should be acquired cannot be considered in a compensation reference arising from a partial acquisition.
material_facts: Only part of the owners’ property, including an outhouse and some open space, was acquired, while the main building and other property remained.
In their application for a compensation reference, the owners claimed additional compensation because the acquisition adversely affected the remaining property.
The High Court granted a request that the remaining property also be acquired, although the matter before it arose from a compensation reference.
issues.conclusion: The request to acquire the entire building could not be entertained in the compensation reference or an appeal arising from it; the High Court’s order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(1) confines a compensation reference to objections about measurement, compensation, the persons to whom compensation is payable, and apportionment. Injury to remaining property may be considered as compensation under section 23(1), but a request to have the whole building acquired under section 49 is a separate remedy and must proceed separately. The Court relied on Pramatha Nath Mullick v. Secretary of State for India in Council, which described the specified grounds of objection under section 18, and distinguished Secretary of State for India in Council v. R. Narayanaswami Chettiar.

predicates.compensation_reference_proceeding: The dispute is being heard as a reference or appeal concerning compensation for acquired property.
predicates.claimant_seeks_entire_building_acquisiti: The claimant asks that the entire building be acquired rather than seeking compensation for the effects of acquiring only part of it.

issues.definition: When a compensation reference concerns acquired property and the claimant asks for the entire building to be acquired, that acquisition request is not considered in the compensation reference.

issues.legal_issue: An owner who wants an entire building acquired instead of only part of it must express that desire before the award is made.
material_facts: The owners did not establish that they had made a request to the acquisition officer for the whole building to be acquired before the award.
The request for acquisition of the remaining property was pursued in proceedings after the award, including in the appeal from the compensation reference.
issues.conclusion: The owners had not taken the required steps before the award to seek acquisition of the whole building, and could not raise that request in the appeal from the compensation reference.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49(1) prohibits proceeding with acquisition of only part of a building when the owner desires the whole building to be acquired; its first proviso permits withdrawal or modification of that expressed desire before the award. The scheme therefore requires the owner to express the desire before the award, with the section 49 procedure remaining distinct from a section 18 reference. The Court approved the approach in Krishna Das Roy v. The Land Acquisition Collector of Pabna and rejected the contrary interpretation in Secretary of State for India in Council v. R. Narayanaswami Chettiar.

predicates.partial_building_acquisition_proceeding: An acquisition proceeding concerns the proposed acquisition of only part of a building.
predicates.owner_wants_entire_building_acquired: The owner wants the whole building acquired instead of only the part proposed for acquisition.
predicates.request_made_after_award: The owner first expresses that desire after the acquisition award has been made.

issues.definition: If only part of a building is proposed for acquisition, an owner who wants the whole building acquired must express that desire before the award; a request first made afterward is untimely.

issues.legal_issue: Damage to an owner’s remaining property caused by an acquisition may be considered in a compensation reference.
material_facts: The acquired property included part of the open space and the outhouses, while the owners’ main building and other property remained.
The owners alleged that the rope-line passed close to the remaining property, making it less useful and causing loss.
The District Judge considered the effect on the remaining property and awarded additional compensation.
issues.conclusion: A claim for additional compensation based on the acquisition adversely affecting the owner’s remaining property may be considered in a compensation reference.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1), including its third and fourth clauses, requires consideration of specified damage caused by severance or by the acquisition injuriously affecting other property or earnings. Such a claim for additional compensation may form the subject matter of a reference under section 18; it is distinct from a request under section 49 to acquire the whole building.

predicates.compensation_reference_proceeding: The dispute is being heard as a reference concerning compensation for acquired property.
predicates.acquisition_injures_remaining_property: The acquisition causes damage to or reduces the utility of property belonging to the owner that was not acquired.
predicates.claimant_seeks_compensation_for_that_inj: The claimant seeks additional compensation for the injury to the remaining property.

issues.definition: In a compensation reference, injury caused by an acquisition to the owner’s remaining property may be considered when the claimant seeks compensation for that injury.
